heroLead: County Line sits exactly where its name suggests, on the Jefferson County border, which means confirming mineral ownership here sometimes starts with figuring out which county's courthouse actually holds the relevant record.
intro: Border communities like this one occasionally have property that was surveyed and recorded inconsistently over the decades, especially for older tracts where the exact county line wasn't always drawn with modern precision. We check both the Jefferson County record and, where a tract sits close enough to the boundary, the neighboring county's records too, before confirming ownership.
We buy interests here directly once that confirmation is complete, and we're upfront with owners about how long the record search takes when a tract sits right on a boundary line.

sections.heading: Why boundary location matters here
paragraphs: A parcel's exact position relative to the county line can affect which courthouse holds its deed and probate history, and in rare cases a tract's legal description has been recorded on both sides historically. We sort that out early so there's no confusion about which records govern your interest.

faqs.question: How do I know which county's records apply to my land near County Line?
faqs.answer: We check the property's legal description against current county boundary maps and, where needed, cross-reference both counties' records to be certain.

faqs.question: Is there mineral activity right around County Line?
faqs.answer: This area sits on the lighter-activity northern edge of the Black Warrior CBM play, so we check current permit records for your specific tract before quoting.

faqs.question: Our deed lists an old legal description that doesn't match modern maps. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Older legal descriptions can usually still be traced and matched to current parcel records, and we handle that as part of confirming ownership.

faqs.question: How long does confirming ownership take when a tract straddles a boundary?
faqs.answer: It can take longer than a straightforward single-county tract, but most cases resolve within a few weeks once both counties' records are checked.
